notes.meaning: Jesus traveled through the towns and villages of Galilee to announce the good news that God's kingdom had arrived. The twelve apostles traveled with Him so they could learn from His teaching and example. Jesus did not stay in one place, but went out to reach ordinary people in both large cities and small country villages.

Several women who had been healed of physical sicknesses and freed from evil spirits also traveled with Jesus. Among them was Mary Magdalene, whom Jesus had delivered from seven demons. Having experienced the Lord's mercy in their own lives, they followed Him with deep thankfulness.

Other women accompanied Jesus, including Joanna, whose husband managed King Herod's household, and Susanna. These women used their own money and goods to provide food and shelter for Jesus and His disciples. Jesus chose a life of poverty, humbly accepting the loving support of His followers as they journeyed.

A massive crowd gathered around Jesus as people traveled from many different towns to hear Him. To teach them important spiritual truths, He told them a parable, which is a story from daily life placed alongside a deeper heavenly lesson. Jesus was ready to teach anyone who was willing to listen.

Jesus began the story with a farmer scattering seed across a field. Some seed landed on the hard footpath running through the ground. Because the ground was packed tight, the seed could not sink in, so passersby walked on it and birds quickly ate it.

Another portion of seed fell onto rocky ground that had only a shallow coating of dirt over stone. The seed sprouted quickly in the warm surface soil. However, as soon as the young plants grew, they dried up and died because the roots had no depth to find water.

Some seed fell into ground where thorn bushes also grew. The weeds grew up right alongside the good plants and took away their light, water, and space. In the end, the thorns smothered the seedlings so they could not produce grain.

The rest of the seed fell into rich, prepared soil. It took root, grew healthy, and produced a huge harvest that was a hundred times what was planted. Jesus then called out loudly, urging everyone who had ears to pay careful attention to the spiritual meaning behind the story.

After hearing the story, Jesus' disciples came to Him to ask what the parable meant. They did not fully understand the lesson on their own, but they had a desire to learn. Jesus welcomed their questions and was glad to explain the truth to those seeking it.

Jesus explained that God had granted His disciples the privilege of understanding the hidden truths of His kingdom. To the wider crowds He spoke in parables so that those who hardened their hearts would hear the story without grasping the deeper meaning. Their lack of understanding showed the spiritual blindness they brought on themselves by ignoring God's truth.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest Luke softened the language of this verse compared to Matthew and Mark so the statement about parables keeping people from understanding would seem less severe.

notes.meaning: Jesus told them plainly that the seed in the story represents the word of God. The seed carries real spiritual life, but it must be planted in human hearts. Just as soil receives physical seed, human hearts are meant to receive God's message.

The seed on the hard path stands for people who hear God's word with closed, careless minds. The devil quickly comes and snatches the message away before it can sink in. He does this because he knows that if they trust the word, they will believe and be saved.

The rocky ground represents people who hear the message and receive it with sudden excitement and joy. But because the truth never puts down deep roots in their inner lives, their belief lasts only for a short time. When hard trials or persecution come, they quickly give up and fall away.

differ.view: True believers are kept by God and can never completely lose their salvation, so the people on rocky ground only had temporary, surface feelings rather than true saving faith.
Some who heard Jesus truly believed in Him for a time, but under testing and trial they stopped believing.

notes.meaning: The seed among thorns stands for people who listen to God's word, but then return to everyday life without guarding their hearts. Daily anxieties, the pursuit of money, and worldly pleasures crowd out the spiritual life. As a result, they never grow to full maturity and produce no real harvest for God.

The seed on good soil represents those with sincere and honest hearts who truly welcome God's word. Instead of letting the truth slip away, they hold fast to it through life's trials. By patiently continuing in obedience, they produce a rich crop of good works and godly character.

A person does not light an oil lamp only to hide it under a clay pot or tuck it beneath a bed. Instead, the lamp is placed high up on a stand so anyone entering the room can see the light. In the same way, the spiritual truth Jesus gives His followers is meant to be shared openly so it guides others.

Jesus taught that nothing hidden will stay concealed forever, for all things will eventually be brought out into the open. The truths He explained privately to His disciples were meant to be made known to the whole world. On the final day, God will also uncover the true condition and motives of every human heart.

Jesus warned His listeners to be very careful about the way they hear God's truth. Whoever values and uses the light they are given will receive even more understanding and blessing. But whoever ignores what they hear will eventually lose even the spiritual knowledge they thought they possessed.

While Jesus was teaching, His mother and brothers arrived wanting to see Him. The crowd packed inside and around the house was so thick that they could not get near Him. They were forced to wait outside while the people listened to Jesus.

differ.view: The brothers mentioned here were younger half-brothers born to Joseph and Mary after Jesus' birth.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Mary remained a virgin throughout her life, so these brothers were either Jesus' cousins or sons of Joseph from an earlier marriage.

notes.meaning: People in the crowd passed word along to Jesus that His family was standing outside. They told Him that His mother and brothers were waiting and wished to speak with Him. Their message was meant to draw Him away from His preaching.

Jesus responded that His true family consists of those who listen to God's word and put it into practice. He was not rejecting His earthly mother and family, but showing that spiritual bonds are even closer than blood relations. Those who obey God are welcomed into the nearest fellowship with Christ.

On a certain day, Jesus instructed His disciples to sail with Him to the other side of the Sea of Galilee. They got into a boat and set out across the water. The disciples obeyed His command, confident because their Master was traveling with them.

As they made their way across the lake, Jesus grew tired from His labors and fell asleep in the boat. Suddenly, a fierce windstorm rushed down the surrounding hills and struck the water. Waves crashed over the sides, filling the boat and placing everyone on board in grave danger.

Terrified by the raging water, the disciples rushed to wake Jesus, crying out that they were about to drown. Jesus got up and spoke directly to the wind and surging waves with divine authority. Instantly the violent storm stopped, and a deep calm settled over the lake.

Jesus asked His disciples why they had failed to trust Him in the middle of the storm. Filled with deep awe and wonder, they asked each other what kind of man He could be. They realized that even the wild winds and waters obeyed His direct command.

After the storm was stilled, they arrived safely on the eastern shore of the lake in the region of the Gerasenes, opposite Galilee. This region was largely Gentile country. Jesus had crossed the water intentionally to bring God's mercy to a place held in spiritual darkness.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Early manuscripts read Gerasenes, Gadarenes, or Gergesenes because ancient copyists and readers often tried to match the location with well-known regional cities such as Gadara or Gerasa.

notes.meaning: As Jesus stepped out onto the shore, a man controlled by demons came out toward Him from the area. For a long time, the evil spirits had driven this man to wear no clothes and avoid living in a house. Instead, he lived alone among graveyard tombs, isolated from human society.

When the man saw Jesus, he fell prostrate before Him, and the demons inside shouted through him with a loud voice. They called Him Jesus, Son of the Most High God, acknowledging His supreme power even while hating Him. Terrified of His judgment, they pleaded with Him not to send them into torment.
